world.title: Ethiopian forces retake Mekelle airport as Tigray rebels retreat
world.summary: Ethiopian federal forces retook Alula Aba Nega Airport in Mekelle and entered the Tigray regional capital, residents and a humanitarian source said Saturday, after more than a week of renewed fighting with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). The federal government had not officially confirmed control of Mekell
world.content: Ethiopian federal forces retook Alula Aba Nega Airport in Mekelle and entered the Tigray regional capital, residents and a humanitarian source said Saturday, after more than a week of renewed fighting with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). The federal government had not officially confirmed control of Mekelle, and communications outages and restricted access made the situation difficult to verify. TPLF fighters’ capture of the airport on Sept. 23 prompted Ethiopian Airlines to suspend flights to Mekelle, Axum and Shire. Federal forces and allied fighters have pushed back a rebel offensive that also reached Afar and Amhara. Reports that TPLF leaders and fighters were leaving Mekelle raised concerns among residents about looting and a security vacuum. A 2022 peace agreement ended the previous two-year war. Ethiopia and Eritrea severed diplomatic ties this week; Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of backing the TPLF, which Eritrea denies. The African Union has urged restraint.

world.title: French student protests spread as police report 5,000 arrests
world.summary: French high school protests over teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and deteriorating buildings have spread nationwide, with about 5,000 people arrested since Monday and more than 600 police officers injured, officials said. Clashes have also injured students and other members of the public, and authorities esti
world.content: French high school protests over teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and deteriorating buildings have spread nationwide, with about 5,000 people arrested since Monday and more than 600 police officers injured, officials said. Clashes have also injured students and other members of the public, and authorities estimate property damage in the tens of millions of euros. Students say schools lack teachers and basic resources and complain of long timetables and poorly maintained facilities. The movement began in Paris-area suburbs and has disrupted hundreds of schools; teachers’ unions have also called for strikes. The government says the education budget will rise by 1.7% in 2027, below inflation, and Education Minister Édouard Geffray has attributed the increase to a falling school-age population. Paris police chief Patrice Faure said protest organizers had lost control and urged a return to peaceful protest, warning that authorities would respond firmly to violence and vandalism. Student organizations have called a nationwide demonstration for Tuesday, October 6, while security officials fear further violence in central Paris.
world.image_alt: French student protests spread as police report 5,000 arrests

world.title: Two Iranian men charged over alleged Manchester Jewish community bomb plot
world.summary: Two Iranian nationals, Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, were charged in Britain on Oct. 2 with preparing terrorist acts in an alleged plot against Manchester’s Jewish community. Prosecutors told a London court that the men conducted reconnaissance of the Heaton Park synagogue and the Jewish Museum and were in
world.content: Two Iranian nationals, Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, were charged in Britain on Oct. 2 with preparing terrorist acts in an alleged plot against Manchester’s Jewish community. Prosecutors told a London court that the men conducted reconnaissance of the Heaton Park synagogue and the Jewish Museum and were in contact with a third person believed to be in Iran who allegedly gave them instructions for making a homemade explosive device. Neither defendant entered a plea, and both were remanded in custody after their Oct. 3 court appearance. The arrests followed an investigation by counterterrorism police and MI5. Police said they believe they disrupted the plot and that it poses no continuing threat to the public. They also said it was not connected to a separate investigation into suspected activity near RAF Fairford. The alleged targets included the Heaton Park synagogue, where two worshippers died in an attack on Oct. 2, 2025. The defendants are due to appear at the Central Criminal Court in London on Oct. 23. Greater Manchester Police said its security plans for Jewish communities would remain in place while the investigation continues.
world.image_alt: Two Iranian men charged over alleged Manchester Jewish community bomb plot

world.title: Latvian PM’s pro-Ukraine party leads with 36.6%, faces coalition talks
world.summary: Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs’ centrist, pro-Ukraine United List party led Latvia’s parliamentary election with 36.6% of the vote after 88% of ballots had been counted, ahead of populist Latvia First at 13.4% and Sovereign Power at 11.6%. United List will still need coalition partners to form a government. The vote fo
world.content: Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs’ centrist, pro-Ukraine United List party led Latvia’s parliamentary election with 36.6% of the vote after 88% of ballots had been counted, ahead of populist Latvia First at 13.4% and Sovereign Power at 11.6%. United List will still need coalition partners to form a government. The vote followed the collapse of the previous coalition in May over its handling of stray military drones that entered Latvian airspace. Officials said the drones came from Ukraine but blamed Russia for diverting them. Security concerns and household costs were prominent campaign issues in the country, which borders Russia and Belarus. Kulbergs has ruled out governing with Latvia First. Exit-poll projections suggested his party and its current coalition partners could together reach 51%, but counting was continuing.

world.title: Israeli strike targeting Hamas official kills five in Gaza apartment
world.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit an apartment building in Gaza City’s Rimal neighbourhood early Saturday, killing at least five Palestinians, including four women, according to hospital and civil defence officials. The dead included Maisa Abu Dawoud and her daughter Mary, both Christians; several other people were wounded. The
world.content: An Israeli airstrike hit an apartment building in Gaza City’s Rimal neighbourhood early Saturday, killing at least five Palestinians, including four women, according to hospital and civil defence officials. The dead included Maisa Abu Dawoud and her daughter Mary, both Christians; several other people were wounded. The Israeli military said it targeted senior Hamas figure Ali al-Amoudi, whom it described as a key operative, and was checking whether he was killed or injured. The strike damaged the building and started a fire. Israel said al-Amoudi was inside an apartment used by Hamas and was involved in planning the Oct. 7, 2023, attack and rebuilding the group. It said it used precision munitions and regretted harm to civilians. Gaza officials and witnesses described civilian casualties and destruction; Hamas has denied Israeli claims that it is rearming or preparing attacks. The attack took place during a ceasefire that took effect in October 2025. Its terms call for Hamas disarmament and an Israeli troop withdrawal, but negotiators have not agreed on conditions for either step. Israel said it was still assessing al-Amoudi’s fate.
world.image_alt: Israeli strike targeting Hamas official kills five in Gaza apartment

world.title: Spain housing protests swell after parliament rejects tenant protections
world.summary: Tens of thousands of people marched in Madrid and cities across Spain on Oct. 3, demanding affordable housing and stronger tenant protections, one day after parliament rejected two emergency decrees from Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s minority government. Madrid authorities estimated 70,000 demonstrators, while organis
world.content: Tens of thousands of people marched in Madrid and cities across Spain on Oct. 3, demanding affordable housing and stronger tenant protections, one day after parliament rejected two emergency decrees from Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s minority government. Madrid authorities estimated 70,000 demonstrators, while organisers said 500,000. The protests followed the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from her Madrid home; her landlord later agreed to let her return at a lower rent. The defeated proposals included extending some rental contracts, restricting evictions of vulnerable tenants and limiting property purchases by investment funds. The Catalan party Junts joined the conservative People’s Party and far-right Vox in voting against them; Junts said the measures lacked rigour. Sánchez’s coalition lacks a parliamentary majority. Opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo called for an early election, while Spanish media reported Sánchez was considering bringing the vote forward; his office declined to comment. The Tenants’ Union said it would discuss a general strike with labour unions.
world.image_alt: Spain housing protests swell after parliament rejects tenant protections

world.title: Coast Guard finds debris from Bermuda-Boston medical flight carrying six
world.summary: The U.S. Coast Guard found a debris field off Nantucket, Massachusetts, from a Canadian-registered air ambulance that lost contact while flying from Bermuda to Boston on Saturday. The Gulfstream G100 carried six people: four Canadian crew members and two Bermudian nationals, a patient and a relative. Search crews conti
world.content: The U.S. Coast Guard found a debris field off Nantucket, Massachusetts, from a Canadian-registered air ambulance that lost contact while flying from Bermuda to Boston on Saturday. The Gulfstream G100 carried six people: four Canadian crew members and two Bermudian nationals, a patient and a relative. Search crews continued looking for them overnight and into Sunday. Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft descending from about 24,000 feet to roughly 11,000 feet before communications stopped. In air traffic control audio, a controller asked whether the pilot was “coming in blind.” Reports citing the recording said the aircraft had electrical problems and declared an emergency, but the pilot’s response was inaudible. Authorities have not confirmed what caused the loss of contact. Latitude Air Ambulance said the crew had flown to Bermuda to collect the patient and a family member. Coast Guard vessels and aircraft continued the search, while Canada’s Transportation Safety Board said it was gathering information about the missing aircraft.
world.image_alt: Coast Guard finds debris from Bermuda-Boston medical flight carrying six

world.title: Bosnia votes in election testing EU path and Dodik’s influence
world.summary: Bosnians went to the polls Sunday to elect the country’s three-member presidency, national and entity lawmakers, and Republika Srpska’s president, with about 3.4 million people eligible to vote. Milorad Dodik, the separatist former Republika Srpska president, is barred from public office but remains influential. His pa
world.content: Bosnians went to the polls Sunday to elect the country’s three-member presidency, national and entity lawmakers, and Republika Srpska’s president, with about 3.4 million people eligible to vote. Milorad Dodik, the separatist former Republika Srpska president, is barred from public office but remains influential. His party is expected to perform strongly in the Serb-majority entity. Problems with new digital equipment delayed voting at some polling stations. The EU opened accession negotiations with Bosnia in 2024, but political blockades have slowed progress. The campaign featured competing calls for a stronger central state, greater Serb autonomy and more Croat influence in choosing the Croat member of the presidency. Authorities introduced biometric voter identification and ballot scanning to address concerns about past irregularities, while voters continue to mark paper ballots. Preliminary results were expected on election night, with the Central Election Commission due to update the count. Coalition talks are likely to determine how the many elected bodies are governed.
world.image_alt: Bosnia votes in election testing EU path and Dodik’s influence

business.content: Two Seeking Alpha analyses offer sharply different assessments of Micron’s memory-chip cycle: one argues the industry peak remains ahead, while the other says the stock-market cycle has already peaked. Bank of America has also revised its Micron stock forecast as the cost of memory used in AI systems rises, TheStreet reported. A linked report says memory executives expect a RAM shortage to continue through 2028. Micron’s fourth-quarter 2026 results beat estimates as demand remained strong.

business.content: About 70 million Social Security and Supplemental Security Income recipients are expected to learn soon how much their benefits will rise in 2027, as the annual cost-of-living adjustment announcement approaches. Higher yields can increase returns on newly purchased fixed-income
business.content: U.S. Treasury yields are near multi-year highs. MarketWatch highlights bond strategies offering a 5% return on cash and reports that financial planners are seeing growing interest in bonds, especially among investors seeking fixed income in retirement. Higher yields can increase returns on newly purchased fixed-income investments and raise government borrowing costs. Fox Business cited a Wall Street Journal headline saying rising government debt was fueling a global bond-market selloff. A Seeking Alpha article offers five reasons yields could stay high and says the bond bull market isn't over; its headline does not specify a forecast period.

business.title: G7 agrees to release 100 million barrels as Trump drops diesel export threat
business.summary: The Group of Seven agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products through the International Energy Agency over four months, starting with a “frontloaded substantial” diesel release within 20 days. The plan follows President Donald Trump’s threat to restrict U.S. diesel exports unless European coun
business.content: The Group of Seven agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products through the International Energy Agency over four months, starting with a “frontloaded substantial” diesel release within 20 days. The plan follows President Donald Trump’s threat to restrict U.S. diesel exports unless European countries drew down their reserves. He said Friday the export ban would not go ahead, and G7 members committed not to restrict energy exports among themselves. The release addresses supply constraints linked to the Iran war and damage to energy infrastructure in Russia and Ukraine. The effect on consumer prices depends on how much diesel is released, when it arrives and whether disrupted supply routes recover. One analyst estimated timely diesel releases could lower U.S. prices by 25 cents a gallon, while another said the effect could be limited. G7 leaders will coordinate the release through the IEA and discuss whether more diesel is needed.
business.image_alt: G7 agrees to release 100 million barrels as Trump drops diesel export threat

business.title: U.S. hemp THC sellers face December ban as Congress weighs rules
business.summary: A federal ban on most intoxicating hemp-derived THC products is set to take effect Dec. 11, threatening a U.S. market estimated at $28 billion. President Donald Trump signed a government-funding measure that delayed the start date from Nov. 12. The delay gives Congress more time to consider regulation instead, as indus
business.content: A federal ban on most intoxicating hemp-derived THC products is set to take effect Dec. 11, threatening a U.S. market estimated at $28 billion. President Donald Trump signed a government-funding measure that delayed the start date from Nov. 12. The delay gives Congress more time to consider regulation instead, as industry advocates seek age limits, THC caps per package and a ban on imported cannabis compounds. The ban would limit hemp products to 0.4 milligrams of THC per container, a threshold industry representatives say could also exclude some CBD items. A market report cited by the industry estimates the ban could displace 225,000 jobs and reduce state sales-tax revenue by $2.1 billion. Opponents and state-licensed cannabis businesses support tighter restrictions, arguing that intoxicating hemp products have been sold with inadequate safeguards and compete with regulated marijuana.
business.image_alt: U.S. hemp THC sellers face December ban as Congress weighs rules

The company’s revenue grew twelvefold to $4.6 billion in fiscal 2025, but it recorded an $8 billion operating loss and a $42 billion total lo
business.content: Anthropic is targeting a $2 trillion valuation for a possible stock-market listing as early as November, a level that would make it one of the largest public offerings on record. The company’s revenue grew twelvefold to $4.6 billion in fiscal 2025, but it recorded an $8 billion operating loss and a $42 billion total loss, including accounting revaluations. Anthropic had planned investments worth more than $500 billion. The company reported infrastructure and computing expenses of $7.3 billion in 2025 and warned that two large customers account for a quarter of revenue. Anthropic could list after the U.S. congressional elections, the article reported.

business.content: The United States is prioritizing shipbuilding with a $66 billion effort to rebuild its industry and expand its naval fleet as China expands its navy, Business Insider reported after visiting a U.S. naval shipyard. China is the world’s leading shipbuilder, and expanding the U.S. fleet will be difficult, the report said. Japanese and South Korean shipbuilders are investing in automated production and deploying robots in “smart shipyards” as concerns about China’s dominance in the industry grow in Washington, the Financial Times reported.

Nvidia’s fiscal second-quarter revenue reached $96.2 billion, while Microsoft’s fiscal 2026 capital
business.content: PwC estimates cumulative global data-center spending could exceed $30 trillion by 2050, while Bain says AI and cloud infrastructure companies need more than $4.2 trillion in new revenue over five years to fund expansion. Nvidia’s fiscal second-quarter revenue reached $96.2 billion, while Microsoft’s fiscal 2026 capital spending rose to $115.9 billion from $64.6 billion a year earlier. science.title: Supreme Court set to hear Boulder climate suit with billions at stake
science.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court is scheduled to hear arguments Monday, Oct. 5, in a lawsuit filed by Boulder, Colorado, seeking damages from ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy for climate-related costs. Boulder says the companies misled the public about their role in climate change and should help pay for local damage. The companies
science.content: The U.S. Supreme Court is scheduled to hear arguments Monday, Oct. 5, in a lawsuit filed by Boulder, Colorado, seeking damages from ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy for climate-related costs. Boulder says the companies misled the public about their role in climate change and should help pay for local damage. The companies and the Trump administration argue that emissions and climate policy are federal matters, not grounds for state-law lawsuits. Local governments have filed dozens of similar lawsuits against oil and gas companies. Boulder filed its suit in 2018, before the 2021 Marshall Fire, which killed two people, destroyed more than 1,000 homes and other structures, and caused an estimated $2 billion in damage. Justice Samuel Alito has recused himself because he owns energy stocks, leaving eight justices and the possibility of a 4-4 tie. The court could also send the case back if it decides it is not ready for review.
science.image_alt: Supreme Court set to hear Boulder climate suit with billions at stake

science.title: Study suggests spaceborne sugar may have helped early life survive
science.summary: A new study explores whether a sugar that arrived from space helped create conditions that allowed it to survive on Earth, where it later became part of the backbone of an important molecule. The study appeared in the journal Scientific Reports. The researchers used conditions on early Earth to investigate how a mixtur
science.content: A new study explores whether a sugar that arrived from space helped create conditions that allowed it to survive on Earth, where it later became part of the backbone of an important molecule. The study appeared in the journal Scientific Reports. The researchers used conditions on early Earth to investigate how a mixture of molecules could support the transition from chemistry to biology.
science.image_alt: Study suggests spaceborne sugar may have helped early life survive

science.title: Molecular-clock study estimates animal origins between 800 million and 700 million years ago
science.summary: An international research team estimates that animals originated between 800 million and 700 million years ago, 100 million to 200 million years before the oldest confirmed animal fossils, which date to about 574 million years ago. The study reassesses molecular-clock calculations by reconsidering maximum-age limits ba
science.content: An international research team estimates that animals originated between 800 million and 700 million years ago, 100 million to 200 million years before the oldest confirmed animal fossils, which date to about 574 million years ago. The study reassesses molecular-clock calculations by reconsidering maximum-age limits based on fossil sites where animals have not been found. Researchers examined three exceptionally well-preserved fossil deposits dated to roughly 850 million to 730 million years ago in Australia, Norway and Arizona. Although conditions at the sites could have preserved early animals, none contained animal fossils. The team used the sites to set revised limits for molecular-clock analyses. The authors say the estimates still depend on difficult interpretations of microscopic fossils and called for further discoveries.
science.image_alt: Molecular-clock study estimates animal origins between 800 million and 700 million years ago

science.title: Google launches satellite to test AI computing in orbit
science.summary: Google’s Project Suncatcher prototype satellite launched into orbit on Oct. 1 to test whether the company’s machine-learning chips can operate in space. A SpaceX rocket carried the satellite, and Planet is expected to bring it online so Google can begin testing the hardware. Google also released a peer-reviewed version
science.content: Google’s Project Suncatcher prototype satellite launched into orbit on Oct. 1 to test whether the company’s machine-learning chips can operate in space. A SpaceX rocket carried the satellite, and Planet is expected to bring it online so Google can begin testing the hardware. Google also released a peer-reviewed version of its white paper on orbital data centers. The mission aims to measure how the chips withstand launch stresses, radiation and extreme temperatures as Google explores solar-powered computing in orbit. Google describes the satellite as an initial test and plans to run the mission for a year.
science.image_alt: Google launches satellite to test AI computing in orbit

science.title: AI researchers warn automated development could trigger rapid intelligence explosion
science.summary: Twenty-two AI researchers from academia, industry and civil society have warned that automating AI research and development could sharply accelerate progress and increase the risk of humans losing control of advanced systems. Their joint paper, released through the University of Cambridge’s AI policy programme, says so
science.content: Twenty-two AI researchers from academia, industry and civil society have warned that automating AI research and development could sharply accelerate progress and increase the risk of humans losing control of advanced systems. Their joint paper, released through the University of Cambridge’s AI policy programme, says some extrapolations suggest that projects now taking months could be automated by mid-2028, though the authors stress that an intelligence explosion is uncertain. The researchers say reduced human involvement could weaken oversight and allow misaligned systems to interfere with successor models or escape containment. They urge governments to measure how far automation has advanced and prepare safeguards before rapid acceleration makes action harder. Their proposals include independent evaluations before companies use systems internally, or embedding external auditors in AI firms. They also identify limits in computing, data and training time, along with the difficulty of automating some work, as possible constraints.
science.image_alt: AI researchers warn automated development could trigger rapid intelligence explosion

science.title: Strong El Niño may worsen droughts, floods and food insecurity
science.summary: A strong El Niño in the Pacific has already surpassed previous records and is forecast to intensify before its usual peak around December. Some experts describe the developing episode as a “super El Niño,” potentially the strongest since the mid-20th century. United Nations estimates cited by El País say drought, flood
science.content: A strong El Niño in the Pacific has already surpassed previous records and is forecast to intensify before its usual peak around December. Some experts describe the developing episode as a “super El Niño,” potentially the strongest since the mid-20th century. United Nations estimates cited by El País say drought, flooding and crop losses linked to the event could push nearly 50 million more people into acute food insecurity. El Niño shifts rainfall patterns: some regions face a greater risk of heavy rain and flooding, while others become drier. The forecast food pressures would add to existing conflicts, debt, cuts to humanitarian aid and geopolitical tensions, El País reported. Forecasters expect the Pacific event to strengthen further before its typical December peak.
science.image_alt: Strong El Niño may worsen droughts, floods and food insecurity

science.title: MEGATRON simulations link JWST galaxies with ancient stellar clues
science.summary: Researchers in the MEGATRON project have published four studies using detailed simulations to trace how the first stars formed, emitted radiation and spread newly forged elements through a young galaxy. The work aims to connect galaxies observed by the James Webb Space Telescope with chemical traces preserved in ancien
science.content: Researchers in the MEGATRON project have published four studies using detailed simulations to trace how the first stars formed, emitted radiation and spread newly forged elements through a young galaxy. The work aims to connect galaxies observed by the James Webb Space Telescope with chemical traces preserved in ancient stars near the Milky Way. The simulations begin with gas containing no heavy elements and track its chemistry and movement as the galaxy grows to roughly the Milky Way’s mass. The team plans to compare more detailed models directly with telescope observations and surveys of old stars. Researchers at the University of Bath have received 40 million processor hours on UK national supercomputers for that work.
science.image_alt: MEGATRON simulations link JWST galaxies with ancient stellar clues

sports.title: Bristol beat reigning champions Northampton 41-26 as Rees-Zammit stars
sports.summary: Bristol Bears beat reigning Premiership champions Northampton Saints 41-26 at Ashton Gate on October 3, with Wales wing Louis Rees-Zammit scoring twice as Bristol made it two wins from two league matches. Bristol scored six tries, including a late penalty try after Tommy Freeman was sin-binned for stopping Rees-Zammit
sports.content: Bristol Bears beat reigning Premiership champions Northampton Saints 41-26 at Ashton Gate on October 3, with Wales wing Louis Rees-Zammit scoring twice as Bristol made it two wins from two league matches. Bristol scored six tries, including a late penalty try after Tommy Freeman was sin-binned for stopping Rees-Zammit from completing a hat-trick. Northampton closed to within eight points after scoring twice in four minutes, but Bristol held on to win. Bristol play Saracens next. Bristol centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg was carried off with a head injury before half-time, then watched the second half from the touchline.
sports.image_alt: Bristol beat reigning champions Northampton 41-26 as Rees-Zammit stars

sports.title: U.S. beat Mexico 3-0 as 17-year-old Sullivan sets scoring record
sports.summary: The United States beat Mexico 3-0 in Glendale on Saturday, with 17-year-old Cavan Sullivan scoring a long-range chip to become the youngest scorer in U.S. men’s national team history. Eighteen-year-old Julian Hall opened the scoring, and Malik Tillman added a late third goal, giving Mauricio Pochettino his first victor
sports.content: The United States beat Mexico 3-0 in Glendale on Saturday, with 17-year-old Cavan Sullivan scoring a long-range chip to become the youngest scorer in U.S. men’s national team history. Eighteen-year-old Julian Hall opened the scoring, and Malik Tillman added a late third goal, giving Mauricio Pochettino his first victory over Mexico as U.S. coach. Mexico controlled the opening stages, but the U.S. settled into the match and capitalized on errors by goalkeeper Raúl Rangel. Mexico defender Mateo Chávez was sent off in the second half. The win was the Americans’ third straight in the international window at the start of the 2030 World Cup cycle. The U.S. is scheduled to close the window against Canada in St. Paul on Tuesday, Oct. 6.
sports.image_alt: U.S. beat Mexico 3-0 as 17-year-old Sullivan sets scoring record

sports.title: Manchester City appeals ruling on Premier League financial breaches
sports.summary: Manchester City has appealed an independent commission’s finding that it breached Premier League financial rules on 114 of 115 charges, contesting a ruling that could lead to sporting and financial penalties. The club lodged the appeal on Thursday evening, Oct. 1, saying the decision contains material errors and that i
sports.content: Manchester City has appealed an independent commission’s finding that it breached Premier League financial rules on 114 of 115 charges, contesting a ruling that could lead to sporting and financial penalties. The club lodged the appeal on Thursday evening, Oct. 1, saying the decision contains material errors and that it is innocent. The commission found that from 2009 to 2018, City used sham commercial arrangements to inflate revenue and reduce costs by more than £900 million, and repeatedly failed to cooperate with the league’s investigation. City denies wrongdoing and says evidence supports its position. No sanction has been set. Possible penalties include a fine, points deduction, transfer ban, removal of titles or expulsion from the Premier League. Any penalty remains subject to the appeal and subsequent disciplinary process. The league says the appeal hearing will remain private until it is permitted to publish the result; rival clubs have pressed for any punishment to take effect this season.
sports.image_alt: Manchester City appeals ruling on Premier League financial breaches

sports.title: Brewers win NLDS opener 3-2 after Padres’ ninth-inning drive hits roof
sports.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the San Diego Padres 3-2 in Game 1 of their National League Division Series on Saturday, Oct. 3, at American Family Field. In the ninth inning, with a runner on and one out, Ty France’s high drive struck a roof cable over fair territory and dropped into left fielder Jackson Chourio’s glove. U
sports.content: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the San Diego Padres 3-2 in Game 1 of their National League Division Series on Saturday, Oct. 3, at American Family Field. In the ninth inning, with a runner on and one out, Ty France’s high drive struck a roof cable over fair territory and dropped into left fielder Jackson Chourio’s glove. Umpires upheld the out after San Diego challenged the call, and Trevor Megill retired Jackson Merrill to end the game. The stadium’s ground rules keep a ball in play if it hits the roof over fair territory, so the review focused on whether the ball was fair or foul—not whether it would have cleared the wall. Milwaukee took a 1-0 lead in the best-of-five series; Game 2 was scheduled for Sunday in Milwaukee.
sports.image_alt: Brewers win NLDS opener 3-2 after Padres’ ninth-inning drive hits roof

sports.content: Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea are monitoring Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic ahead of the January transfer window, with reports putting the Croatian forward’s asking price at about £50 million. The reports describe interest, not a confirmed bid. United have discussed him internally, while Arsenal and Chelsea have sent representatives to watch him, according to CaughtOffside, as cited in the reports. Matanovic, 23, has scored six goals in his first seven appearances across competitions this season, prompting Freiburg’s reported valuation to rise from around £30 million over the summer. Arsenal did not add a recognised centre-forward in the summer, while Chelsea has focused on young players with development potential. Matanovic scored 15 goals for Freiburg last season.

sports.content: Republic of Ireland officials abruptly ended head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson’s pre-match press conference in Bačka Topola, Serbia, on Saturday after Israeli journalists questioned him about an alleged attack aboard a Flydubai flight and accused Irish players of racially abusing opponents. The Football Association of Ireland’s communications chief, Kieran Crowley, called the racism allegation “completely untrue”; the claim has not been independently established. The confrontation took place before the teams’ Nations League rematch on Sunday, October 4, following Ireland’s 3-0 win in their first meeting on September 27. Both fixtures have drawn protests and debate in Ireland over the Gaza war. The FAI moved Ireland’s home fixture out of the country, citing security concerns. Hallgrimsson said reports from both teams would go through the relevant processes and that he wanted attention to return to football. The Israel Football Association had not filed a complaint with UEFA over the racism allegation but said it would consider doing so after Sunday’s match.

sports.content: Jannik Sinner withdrew from the Shanghai Masters because of a persistent knee injury as Alexander Zverev pursues the year-end world No. 1 ranking. Zverev, currently ranked second, would need to win both the China Open in Beijing and Shanghai to overtake Sinner, who has not played since beating Zverev in the Wimbledon final in July. Zverev advanced to the Beijing quarter-finals on Saturday with a 6-0, 6-3 win over China’s Juncheng Shang in 55 minutes, setting up a Sunday meeting with Novak Djokovic. Shanghai runs from October 7 to 18. The ranking race also depends on the points Sinner must defend from his late-season titles last year. Zverev won the French Open and US Open this season and reached the Australian Open semi-finals and Wimbledon final. Winning both Beijing and Shanghai would make him the first German man to lead the ATP rankings since Boris Becker in 1991.

sports.content: West Indies chased down India’s 351-7 to win the third one-day international by five wickets in New Chandigarh, with captain Shai Hope’s unbeaten 162 leading the team to its highest successful ODI chase. The visitors reached 352-5 with 10 balls to spare, but India had already secured the three-match series and finished it 2-1. India recovered from 4-2, with Rohit Sharma scoring 92 and Ruturaj Gaikwad 57 in a 137-run partnership. KL Rahul then added an unbeaten 129. Hope kept wicket for India’s 50 overs before opening the chase after Jewel Andrew injured a finger in the field. Despite a groin injury, Hope batted on and hit 40 runs from his final 16 deliveries. Hope’s innings denied India a clean sweep after wins in the first two matches. India and West Indies begin a five-match T20 series in Lucknow on Tuesday.
